articles.title: A Randomized Phase III Trial of Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy Followed by Durvalumab Consolidation, With or Without Induction Chemo-Immunotherapy, in Patients With Unresectable Locally Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: JCOG2510 (PRIME-CRT).
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) followed by durvalumab consolidation is the current standard of care for unresectable locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (LA-NSCLC). However, survival outcomes in this setting remain unsatisfactory. Although the PACIFIC trial improved outcomes, further intensification of systemic therapy may be required to improve long-term survival. Preclinical and perioperative clinical evidence suggests that introducing immunotherapy in the presence of an intact primary tumor may enhance antitumor immune responses. Recently, early-phase studies have reported the feasibility and potential efficacy of induction chemo-immunotherapy followed by cCRT; however, its clinical benefit has not been confirmed in a phase III trial. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, phase III trial is designed to determine whether the addition of induction chemo-immunotherapy to the current standard strategy of cCRT followed by durvalumab consolidation improves survival outcomes in patients with unresectable LA-NSCLC. Previously untreated patients with unresectable LA-NSCLC without activating EGFR mutations are randomized 1:1 to receive either cCRT followed by durvalumab consolidation or induction chemo-immunotherapy followed by cCRT and durvalumab consolidation. Randomization is adjusted for age, clinical stage, programmed death-ligand 1 expression, and institution. The primary endpoints are progression-free and overall survival. Secondary endpoints include objective response rate, proportion of patients proceeding to cCRT after induction therapy, and adverse events. A total of 212 patients will be enrolled from 60 institutions over 5 years. CONCLUSION: The results of this trial should clarify whether the addition of induction chemo-immunotherapy can enhance curative potential and lead to improved overall survival in patients with unresectable LA-NSCLC.

articles.title: Stage II Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Upfront Surgery or Neoadjuvant Chemoimmunotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy adoption in stage II non-small cell lung cancer is shrouded by lack of clear survival advantages and stratification across randomized clinical trials. METHODS: An individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis was conducted comparing overall survival of stage II patients (according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer TNM staging, eighth edition) receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in phase 3 randomized controlled trials with overall survival of patients undergoing upfront surgery included in the pathologic eighth and ninth edition TNM databases. Individual patient data were extracted using the individual patient data from Kaplan-Meier survival curves (IPDfromKM) method. Cox regression analyses estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and relative 95% (CIs). Meta-analysis and metaregression comparing neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy and chemotherapy were also conducted. Relative risk (RR) with 95% CI was derived. RESULTS: Overall survival IPD were extracted from 275 stage II patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy and from 6864 (eighth edition) and 7342 (ninth edition) patients undergoing upfront surgery in the pathologic TNM-database. Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy improved survival compared with upfront surgery in the eighth edition TNM database (HR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.53-0.87; P = .002) but yielded similar survival compared with the ninth edition (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.64-1.1; P = .10). Compared with chemotherapy, pathologic complete response (RR, 6.19; 95% CI, 3.37-10.27; P < .001) and major pathologic response (RR, 3.08; 95% CI, 2.27-4.16; P < .001) favored neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Similarly, chemoimmunotherapy improved event-free survival (HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.52-0.82; P 0.001) and overall survival (HR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50-0.92; P = .01). Similar rates of canceled surgery, open surgery, pneumonectomy, conversion from minimally invasive to open surgery, and positive margin were found. The percentage of stage II patients did not modulate surgical-related adverse events, 90-day mortality, and adjuvant treatment receipt. CONCLUSIONS: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy has encouraging results in stage II lung cancer, but stratification tools are warranted to select high-risk patients. Compared with chemotherapy, chemoimmunotherapy improves both long-term outcomes and pathologic response with comparable surgical outcomes.

articles.title: Two-year outcomes following PSMA PET and MRI guided prostate SABR with simultaneous focal boost: a brief report from the ARGOS-CLIMBER phase 1/2 trial.
articles.abstract: ARGOS-CLIMBER is a phase 1/2 trial evaluating PSMA PET and MRI guided prostate SABR with a simultaneous boost to intraprostatic and nodal disease in men with unfavourable intermediate and high-risk prostate cancer. The updated results demonstrate acceptable safety and quality of life with high biochemical and imaging response rates.
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology

articles.title: Photobiomodulation for radiotherapy-induced dysgeusia in head and neck cancer patients: a pilot randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Dysgeusia is a frequent complication in patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) undergoing radiotherapy and may negatively affect nutritional status and quality of life. This pilot study evaluated the effect of photobiomodulation (PBM) on the management of radiotherapy-induced dysgeusia. Sixteen patients undergoing radiotherapy for HNC were randomly assigned to either a PBM group (n = 8) or a zinc sulfate group (n = 8). Objective taste identification tests evaluating sweet, bitter, sour, and salty tastes were performed at three time points: before radiotherapy (T0), at the 15th radiotherapy session (T1), and at the 30th radiotherapy session (T2). Salty taste was the most affected taste modality in both groups. At T2, sweet taste was correctly identified by 75.0% of patients in the zinc group and 50.0% in the PBM group. In contrast, bitter taste was preserved in 87.5% of patients in the PBM group and 75.0% in the zinc group. Sour taste was preserved in 87.5% and 62.5% of patients in the PBM and zinc groups, respectively, whereas salty taste was preserved in 50.0% and 25.0% of patients, respectively. No statistically significant differences were observed between groups at T0, T1, or T2 (all p > 0.05). Although no statistically significant differences were identified, PBM was associated with better preservation of sour, bitter, and salty taste perception, particularly after the 30th radiotherapy session. These preliminary findings suggest that PBM may represent a promising supportive strategy for the management of treatment-related dysgeusia in patients with HNC undergoing radiotherapy.

articles.title: Geographic and Sex Distribution of LI-RADS Research Globally: A Cross-Sectional Meta-Research Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has an uneven global distribution and a higher incidence in males. The Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (LI-RADS) is a standardized imaging framework for HCC diagnosis. It is unclear whether the evidence used to inform LI-RADS reflects the global burden of HCC. PURPOSE: To determine whether the geographic and sex distribution of studies assessing LI-RADS and those included in the LI-RADS individual participant data (IPD) database reflect the global burden of HCC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional meta-research study comparing the country- and sex-specific HCC prevalence from GLOBOCAN 2022 with the distribution of studies eligible for and included in the LI-RADS IPD database. Studies were identified through a systematic search of 4 databases. RESULTS: We identified 470 eligible studies including 98 014 patients; of these, 76 studies comprising 11 924 patients were included in the IPD database. Asian and African countries, excluding Republic of Korea, were underrepresented in both the eligible and the IPD dataset. North America was overrepresented. Female patients were under-represented in LI-RADS eligible studies ( CONCLUSION: LI-RADS research is disproportionately reported from some countries relative to HCC burden. Asia, Africa, and female patients remain underrepresented. This may affect the generalizability and diagnostic equity of the LI-RADS system and underscore the need for improved global inclusivity in LI-RADS research. CONTEXTE :: la répartition mondiale du carcinome hépatocellulaire (CHC) est inégale, avec une incidence plus élevée chez les hommes. Le système LI-RADS (système de compte rendu et de données de l’imagerie hépatique) est un cadre d’imagerie standardisé pour le diagnostic du CHC. On ignore cependant si les données probantes utilisées pour étayer le LI-RADS reflètent le fardeau mondial du CHC. OBJECTIF :: déterminer si la répartition géographique et selon le sexe des études évaluant le système LI-RADS, ainsi que celle des études incluses dans la base de données individuelles des participants (IPD) de LI-RADS, reflètent le fardeau mondial du CHC. MATÉRIEL ET MÉTHODES :: nous avons mené une étude transversale de méta-recherche comparant la prévalence du CHC par pays et par sexe selon GLOBOCAN 2022 à la répartition des études admissibles à la base de données IPD de LI-RADS et de celles qui y ont été incluses. Les études ont été identifiées par une recherche systématique dans quatre bases de données. Protocole de l’étude : RÉSULTATS :: nous avons identifié 470 études admissibles ayant inclus 98 014 patients. Parmi ces études, 76 études regroupant 11 924 patients ont été incluses dans la base de données IPD. Les pays asiatiques (à l’exclusion de la République de Corée) et africains étaient sous-représentés dans les études admissibles et dans la base de données IPD. L’Amérique du Nord était surreprésentée. Les patientes étaient sous-représentées dans les études admissibles sur LI-RADS (Z = -21,95; CONCLUSION :: la recherche sur LI-RADS provient de manière disproportionnée de certains pays par rapport au fardeau du CHC. L’Asie, l’Afrique et les patientes (femmes) demeurent sous-représentées. Cela pourrait nuire à la généralisabilité du système LI-RADS ainsi qu’à l’équité diagnostique, et souligne le besoin d’améliorer l’inclusivité à l’échelle mondiale dans la recherche sur LI-RADS.
articles.journal: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes

articles.title: TIM3 Blockade with Hypomethylating Therapy Restores NK Cell and Cytotoxic CD4+ T-cell Activity in Patients with AML or MDS.
articles.abstract: Occasional complete responses (CR) to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy demonstrate that acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) can be immunosensitive when appropriately targeted. In this study, we analyzed patients with AML/MDS (n = 14) who were treated with the anti-TIM3 sabatolimab and the hypomethylating agent decitabine in a phase Ib clinical trial (NCT03066648) using single-cell RNA and T-cell receptor (TCR) sequencing (n = 6) and functional coculture assays. Unlike T cell-restricted CTLA4 and PD1, TIM3 was broadly expressed across natural killer (NK) cell, myeloid cell, and T-cell populations. Therapy induced the expansion of cytotoxic NK cell subsets and enhanced type I IFN signaling. Fewer than 1% of bone marrow CD8+ T cells displayed a canonical exhaustion phenotype, and treatment preferably expanded small CD8+ T-cell clones in responders. Responders exhibited greater expansion of cytotoxic CD4+ T cells and B cells, as exemplified by a patient with preexisting CD4+ T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia (T-LGLL) achieving an outstanding CR lasting 23 months. More than 20% of this patient's lymphocytes were T-LGLL cells expressing a TCR capable of recognizing autologous blasts. Overall, our results suggest that anti-TIM3 combined with decitabine engages a distinct mechanism of immune activation compared with anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA4, preferentially expanding NK cell and CD4+ T-cell populations.

articles.title: Secondary Ophthalmic Artery Chemotherapy for Bilateral Retinoblastoma After Incomplete Response to Intravenous Chemotherapy: Initial Prospective Experience from a Resource-Limited Setting.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ophthalmic artery chemotherapy (OAC) is increasingly used for globe salvage in retinoblastoma, but prospective evidence from low- and middle- income countries is scarce. We evaluated short-term outcomes of secondary OAC after insufficient response to intravenous chemotherapy (IVC) with/without focal therapy in a resource- limited setting. MATERIALS & METHODS: In this prospective study (January 2023-June 2025), 21 eyes (5 group B, 5 group C, 8 group D, 3 group E) from 20 children with bilateral retinoblastoma were included; 19 had prior unilateral enucleation. Thirteen eyes underwent bridging OAC after partial IVC response, and eight received rescue OAC for failure or recurrence. Primary endpoints were globe salvage, tumor control, and complications. RESULTS: The cohort included 12 males (60%); median age at diagnosis was 11 months (IQR: 4-18) and at OAC initiation 27 months (IQR: 17-36.5). Eighty-one OAC sessions were delivered (median 4 per eye, IQR: 3-5). After median follow-up of 19 months, overall globe salvage was 76.2% (16/21). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed eye preservation >80% at 12 months and ~70% at 24 months. Complications with permanent sequelae occurred in only one case (5%), with no mortality. Recurrence was observed in 23.5%. Exploratory subgroup analysis showed higher observed globe salvage with among eyes receiving bridging OAC than with among those receiving rescue OAC (100% vs. 37.5%); . However, this finding should be interpreted cautiously because of differences in the two groups differed in baseline disease characteristics, behavior, treatment indication, and underlying chemosensitivity between groups, and the observed association may reflect these factors rather than the timing of OAC alone. Lack of a favorable response after the first OAC cycle was associated with subsequent enucleation (RR = 6.00, 95% CI 1.03-35.91, p=0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This prospective single-center study suggests that secondary OAC is a feasible globe-preserving treatment after incomplete response to IVC with/without focal thrapy in a resource-limited setting. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested higher observed globe salvage with bridging OAC and an association between lack of response after the first OAC session and subsequent enucleation; however, findings should be interpreted cautiously because of small sample size and potential confounding by treatment indication and baseline tumor biology. Larger multicenter studies with longer follow-up are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Effects of exercise and educational programs on long-term quality of life, anxiety, and depression in breast cancer survivors: an exploratory secondary analysis of the Setouchi breast project-10 randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Advances in early detection and multimodal therapy have increased the population of long-term breast cancer survivors, underscoring the importance of survivorship care focused on health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Although exercise and educational interventions show short-term benefits, their long-term sustainability remains unclear. This study evaluated the longitudinal effects of these interventions on HRQoL and psychological outcomes after initial treatment. METHODS: This secondary analysis of the Setouchi Breast Project-10 randomized controlled trial included 342 patients with stage 0-III breast cancer within one year of treatment completion, assigned to usual care (n = 114), education (n = 120), or exercise (n = 108). HRQoL was assessed using FACT-B and its subscales, and psychological outcomes using HADS at baseline and 2, 4, 6, and 12 months. Responder analyses based on minimally important differences and mixed-effects models for repeated measures were conducted. RESULTS: The education group showed greater early improvement in the FACT-B Trial Outcome Index at 2 months versus control (51% vs. 32%, p = 0.003). Although MID analyses suggested deterioration in some global domains at 12 months in the exercise group, longitudinal analyses demonstrated sustained improvement in the breast cancer subscale in both intervention groups. No consistent between-group differences were observed in global HRQoL or HADS scores. CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory secondary analysis suggests that physician-led educational interventions and structured exercise may contribute to maintaining breast cancer-specific HRQoL, particularly in disease-specific domains. However, global HRQoL and psychological outcomes did not show consistent improvements, and a tendency toward deterioration was observed in some indicators for the exercise group at 12 months. These findings should be interpreted with caution, but they suggest that low-cost educational approaches could be a resource-efficient option in survivorship care.

articles.title: Safety and Performance of the Colovac Anastomosis Protection Device. A Pooled Analysis of Prospective Studies Compared With Diverting Loop Ileostomy (SAFE-2025).
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the safety and effectiveness of the Colovac Anastomosis Protection Device with standard diverting ostomy (DO) following low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer. SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: DO is standard of care (SOC) following LAR for rectal cancer but is associated with substantial morbidity. Colovac Device is designed to divert the fecal stream away from the anastomosis intraluminally. METHODS: Three prospective multicenter Colovac trials were pooled and compared with a prospective cohort of patients undergoing LAR with DO for rectal cancer using a propensity score-weighted approach to balance baseline characteristics. The primary safety endpoint for both Colovac and SOC trials was the rate of device-related or stoma-related early major complications by POD10. Secondary endpoints included early anastomotic leak (AL) rates, fecal stream diversion effectiveness, and device migration. RESULTS: Patients were included (Colovac=49, DO=54). By POD10, device- or stoma-related major complications rates were 4.1% (2/49) vs 5.6% (3/54) ( P =0.167). All Colovac devices were successfully placed and retrieved with stoma avoidance achieved in 83.7% at POD10. Major complication rates were similar between groups. Rates of AL detected on POD9/10 were comparable between Colovac and control patients (28.6% vs. 20.4%, P =0.102), with total AL rate of 32.6% in Colovac versus 27.8% ( P =0.342) in control at POD30. Effective fecal diversion was achieved in 91.7% of Colovac patients, with device migration in 14.3%. CONCLUSIONS: Colovac enabled ostomy avoidance in most patients without increasing major complications or AL, suggesting its role as a potential alternative to DO following LAR for rectal cancer. TRIAL REGISTRATION: SAFE-2019: NCT05180565; SAFE-2: NCT05010850; SAFE-2023: NCT06540807; SH-SOC23: NCT06152276.

articles.title: LEgal Guidance for Cancer Patients and CAREgivers (LEGACY CARE): A Pilot Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Medical-legal partnerships can address health-harming legal needs (HHLNs) but caregiver-inclusive models are understudied. AIMS: To evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy in addressing HHLNs of proactive legal care for patient-caregiver dyads. METHODS: This single-arm pilot trial (NCT07153016) enrolled patients with advanced-stage colorectal cancer and their self-nominated caregiver. Cancer Legal Care (CLC) provided personalized legal checkups and 3-month follow-up at no cost. Feasibility was assessed by rates of initial checkup, 3-month engagement, and receipt of legal service. Acceptability was assessed by likelihood of recommending the intervention to others. Participant-reported outcomes, implementation measures, and interviews were summarized. RESULTS: We enrolled 9 of 10 planned dyads. Among the 9 enrolled, 8 completed baseline surveys, 7 completed initial legal checkups, and 7 completed 3-month assessments. Initial legal checkups lasted a median of 45 minutes, and CLC provided median 4 hours of legal service per dyad. At baseline, 7 of 16 participants self-identified HHLNs, while CLC identified 1.7 additional HHLNs per dyad. The study met predefined feasibility benchmarks [initial engagement (16/18, 89%), 3-month questionnaire completion (14/18, 78%), and receipt of ≥ 1 legal service (14/18, 78%)] and acceptability (12/14, 86% recommended the intervention) benchmarks. Dyads noted improvements in financial control, support-seeking, and maintaining daily activities; however, caregiver-specific needs were not consistently identified or prioritized. CONCLUSIONS: Proactive legal care for recently diagnosed patient-caregiver dyads was feasible and acceptable, and identified and addressed HHLNs. However, caregiver-inclusive medical-legal partnership models may require caregiver-specific intake, longitudinal follow-up, and clearer distinction between patient, caregiver, and shared needs.

articles.title: Comparison of Traumatic Complications following Prostate Biopsy in Men with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Due to Prostate Disease Using Biopty Gun versus Semiautomatic Needle.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prostate biopsy has evolved to improve yield and reduce complications. The development of biopty guns added to this trend. It is an improvement on the semiautomatic needle. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare semi-automatic and fully-automatic biopsy devices used for digitally guided transrectal prostate biopsy for the rate and extent of post-biopsy pain and bleeding complications. METHODOLOGY: Sixty-four patients were randomised into two groups, each with 32 patients. Group 1 patients were biopsied with 16G Medplus ® semi-automatic biopsy needles, whereas Bard-Magnum ® biopty gun with 16G needles was used for Group 2. Twelve systematic cores were taken from both groups. Post-biopsy pain was assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale and Wong-Baker Faces Pain Rating Scale. The rate and extent of post-biopsy haematuria/urethral bleeding and rectal bleeding were evaluated. Data were collected using a structured pro forma and analysed using IBM-SPSS. RESULTS: Sixty-four men participated in the study. Haematuria/urethral bleeding occurred in 37.5% (12) and 31.25% (10) patients in Groups 1 and 2, respectively. Bladder irrigation was done for 8.3% (1) and 20% (2) of those who bled from Groups 1 and 2, respectively. Significant rectal bleeding occurred in 31.25% (10) and 28.13% (9) patients from Groups 1 and 2, respectively. More pain was noted in Group 1. These differences in bleeding complications and pain were not statistically significant. CONCLUSION: The two devices did not exhibit significant differences in terms of pain or bleeding complications when used for prostate biopsy.

articles.title: Predictors of Enrolment in a Transoral Surgical Trial for HPV-Related Oropharyngeal Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated demographic, clinical and perceptual factors associated with enrolment in a Phase III transoral surgical trial for HPV-related oropharyngeal carcinoma. DESIGN: Single-centre, questionnaire-based cross-sectional pilot study of patients screened for PATHOS trial. SETTING: Tertiary cancer centre participating in the PATHOS trial. PARTICIPANTS: Patients with p16-positive oropharyngeal carcinoma were eligible for the trial. Of 100 patients screened, 70 met trial eligibility and 51 completed a telephone questionnaire and were included. Inability to complete the questionnaire because of cognitive impairment or a language barrier was a prespecified survey exclusion criterion. However, no patient was excluded for either reason. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcome was the patient decision to enrol or decline participation in PATHOS (written consent). Predictor variables included demographic and clinical characteristics and responses to a 31-item Likert-scale questionnaire. RESULTS: Among 51 eligible patients who completed the questionnaire, 29 (57%) enroled in the trial. On univariable analysis, significant predictors included perceptions of treatment quality, toxicity, quality of life, travel distance, trial comprehension, randomisation, medical terminology, trust, prior trial experience and concern about being treated as a 'guinea pig'. On multivariable analysis, prior trial experience (p = 0.022) and not feeling like a 'guinea pig' (p = 0.047) remained significant, with travel distance trending (p = 0.087). CONCLUSIONS: Trial enrolment was driven primarily by prior exposure to clinical research and perceptions of vulnerability and trust, rather than by demographic or tumour factors. Addressing fears of being a 'guinea pig', improving trial comprehension and mitigating travel-related barriers may enhance accrual and promote more equitable participation in head and neck cancer trials.
articles.journal: Clinical otolaryngology : official journal of ENT-UK ; official journal of Netherlands Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology & Cervico-Facial Surgery

articles.title: Specialist Referral for Cardiovascular Risk in Patients With Prostate Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Patients with prostate cancer have a high burden of cardiovascular risk factors, often suboptimally controlled, and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether the routine referral of patients with prostate cancer to a cardiovascular specialist to implement a systematic risk factor strategy is more likely to reduce adverse cardiovascular outcomes and improve risk factor control than usual care. DESIGN, SETTINGS, AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized clinical trial included patients with prostate cancer from 55 sites in 8 countries between 2015 and 2025. Eligible patients were diagnosed with prostate cancer during the past 12 months; had received treatment with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for the first time within the past 6 months; or planned to start ADT in the next month. Patients taking a statin with a systolic blood pressure of 130 mm Hg or lower were ineligible. Data were analyzed from May 25 to August 7, 2026. INTERVENTION: Patients were allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive usual care alone or usual care plus routine referral to an internist or cardiologist. The specialists provided a systematic intervention, including a target of systolic blood pressure of 130 mm Hg or lower and a statin medication, irrespective of the patient's cholesterol levels (even if not usual or guideline-driven practice); encourage smoking cessation; and provide guidance on diet and exercise. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Hierarchical composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, suboptimal cholesterol (total cholesterol, >155 mg/dL [to convert to mmol/L, multiply by 0.0259]) and suboptimal blood pressure (systolic blood pressure, >130 mm Hg) as evaluated by the win ratio. RESULTS: The analysis included 2487 patients with prostate cancer (mean [SD] age, 68 [8] years). During median (IQR) follow-up of 5.8 (2.7-8.2) years, the win ratio in favor of the intervention was 1.60 (95% CI, 1.42-1.81), mostly attributable to lower cholesterol in the intervention group (mean difference, 12 mg/dL; 95% CI, 9-15 mg/dL) as a consequence of greater protocol-mandated statin use. Mean (SD) close-out systolic blood pressure values were 131.1 (16.9) mm Hg in the intervention group and 132.9 (18.3) mm Hg in the control group. There was no difference in time to cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure between groups (subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.79-1.49). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, routine referral of patients with prostate cancer to a cardiovascular specialist lead to improved outcomes, specifically through better cholesterol control. However, it is uncertain whether this reduced clinical cardiovascular events. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03127631.

articles.title: Sex difference in survival benefits of immune checkpoint inhibitors in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether sex influences the survival benefit of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains uncertain. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus up to April 1, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing ICIs with chemotherapy and reporting overall survival (OS) or progression-free survival (PFS) stratified by sex. A random-effects model was used for meta-analysis. RESULTS: Sixty-three publications (reporting 42 phase 3 RCTs) involving 25,827 patients (18,772 male; 7,055 female) were included. Compared with chemotherapy, ICIs significantly improved both OS and PFS in males (OS: HR 0.74 [95% CI 0.71-0.78]; PFS: HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.54-0.64]) and females (OS: HR 0.83 [95% CI 0.77-0.90]; PFS: HR 0.76 [95% CI 0.66-0.86]). Pooled treatment-by-sex interaction analyses demonstrated significantly greater OS (interaction HR = 0.90 [95% CI 0.84-0.97]; P = 0.01) and PFS (interaction HR = 0.82 [95% CI 0.73-0.92]; P = 0.0006) benefits in males than in females. In subgroup analyses, sex‑based differences in OS reached statistical significance in patients receiving ICI monotherapy (P = 0.02), including those treated with anti‑PD‑1 monotherapy (P = 0.04) and those with PD‑L1 expression ≥50% (P = 0.02). However, these differences did not persist after the False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction (adjusted P = 0.07, 0.10, and 0.07, respectively). In contrast, sex‑based differences in PFS remained statistically significant after FDR correction in the ICI monotherapy (adjusted P = 0.001), anti‑PD‑1 monotherapy (adjusted P = 0.001), and PD‑L1 ≥ 50% (adjusted P = 0.004) subgroups. No significant sex‑based differences in either OS or PFS were observed among patients treated with ICI plus chemotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: Although ICIs are superior to chemotherapy in both sexes, the PFS benefit of ICI monotherapy appears to be attenuated in females relative to males. Given the imbalances in baseline confounders coupled with the underrepresentation of females in the included trials, these findings should be interpreted with caution and warrant confirmation in future RCTs designed specifically to investigate sex‑based differences.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant Therapy in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: Current Evidence, Evolving Strategies, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Neoadjuvant therapy is now a cornerstone of muscle-invasive bladder cancer management, evolving from traditional cisplatin-based chemotherapy to novel immunotherapy and antibody-drug conjugate combinations. While dose-dense methotrexate, vinblastine, doxorubicin, and cisplatin remains the cytotoxic standard, the phase III NIAGARA and KEYNOTE 905 trials have established new benchmarks for cisplatin-eligible and ineligible populations, respectively. Furthermore, the integration of molecular subtyping, DNA damage repair biomarkers, and liquid biopsies (circulating tumor DNA) is facilitating a shift toward precision medicine. These advancements aim to optimize pathologic response, improve overall survival, and identify candidates for bladder-sparing approaches.
articles.journal: The Urologic clinics of North America

articles.title: Symptom-guided reduction of BCG dwell time: findings from the north-REG randomized trial.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of personalized dwell-time (DT) reductions on symptom prevalence and systemic toxicities in patients undergoing Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) instillation for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). METHODS: Within a multinational randomized controlled trial (North-REG Dwell Time Study [NCT04701151]), 225 patients provided daily electronic patient-reported outcomes data during BCG induction and maintenance cycles. Participants were randomized 1:1, stratified by clinical site, sex, and concomitant carcinoma in situ, to either a standard care arm (control) or an intervention arm. Toxicity was analysed using a 'worst-day' principle to capture peak symptom burden. All patients initially received a standard 120-min DT. In the intervention group, algorithm-guided DT reductions (to 60 or 30 min) were triggered by real-time symptom severity, whereas the control group maintained a 120-min DT. RESULTS: At baseline, 69% vs. 71% (control vs. intervention) of participants reported pre-existing symptoms, primarily lower urinary tract symptoms such as pollakiuria and urgency. During induction, the intervention group experienced significantly lower rates of urgency at week 3 (34% vs. 47%, P = 0.04) and week 6 (32% vs. 49%, P = 0.01). Significant reductions were also observed during maintenance at week 9 for systemic symptoms (30% vs. 61%, P < 0.001) and fatigue (22% vs. 47%, P = 0.001). Total adherence to the 15-instillation protocol was 38% in the intervention group and 40% in the control group. CONCLUSION: Daily electronic patient-reported outcomes monitoring revealed that patients with NMIBC have a high baseline symptom burden prior to BCG therapy. Symptom-guided DT reductions may reduce local urgency and systemic toxicity and improve treatment tolerability. However, treatment completion does not seem to be affected.

articles.title: Extraoral Versus Intraoral Photobiomodulation for the Prevention of Oral Mucositis in Pediatric Patients Undergoing High-Dose Methotrexate Chemotherapy.
articles.abstract: AIMS: To compare intraoral (IO) and extraoral (EO) photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) for preventing oral mucositis (OM) in pediatric patients receiving high-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX). METHODS AND RESULTS: This prospective, open-label, randomized clinical trial included 75 HD-MTX treatment episodes from 31 pediatric patients aged 1-18 years. Each episode was randomized to IO-PBMT or EO-PBMT with red light at 660 nm. Preventive PBMT was initiated before HD-MTX infusion and administered daily until discharge. OM was assessed at baseline and on days 3, 5, and 10 using the World Health Organization scale. Pain, salivary pH, and salivary biochemical profiles were secondary or exploratory outcomes. Cumulative OM occurred in 22/37 IO-PBMT episodes (59.5%) and 12/38 EO-PBMT episodes (31.6%). After accounting for repeated episodes within patients, OM risk was higher with IO-PBMT (risk ratio, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.07-3.19; p = 0.029). Pain scores, salivary pH, and biochemical profiles did not differ significantly between groups. EO-PBMT required substantially less application time, and no adverse effects were reported. CONCLUSION: EO-PBMT was associated with lower cumulative OM occurrence, shorter application time, and good tolerability, supporting its use as a promising, less burdensome preventive strategy in pediatric oncology.
articles.journal: Special care in dentistry : official publication of the American Association of Hospital Dentists, the Academy of Dentistry for the Handicapped, and the American Society for Geriatric Dentistry

articles.title: Neoadjuvant concurrent or sequential anthracycline-containing chemotherapy and HER2-targeted agents for HER2-positive breast cancer: a randomized phase 2 study (METIS).
articles.abstract: The integration of anthracyclines with HER2-targeted agents in neoadjuvant therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer has been limited by cardiotoxicity concerns. This randomized phase II METIS trial (NCT04172259) assessed whether concurrent pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (PLD)-containing chemotherapy plus dual HER2 blockade (trastuzumab/pertuzumab) could improve efficacy without increasing cardiac risk. A total of 156 patients with stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer were randomized to a PLD-based concurrent regimen or an epirubicin and cyclophosphamide (EC)-based sequential regimen. The PLD-based concurrent group achieved a higher pathological complete response (pCR) rate (67.5% vs. 48.7%; difference, 18.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.6-34.0; P = 0.033) compared with the EC-based sequential group, with greater benefit in hormone receptor-positive disease (58.7% vs. 36.7%) and stage II tumors (82.1% vs. 48.0%). After a median follow-up of 37.5 months, fewer event-free survival (EFS) events occurred in the PLD-based concurrent group (3 vs. 8), yielding a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.35 (95% CI, 0.09-1.32; P = 0.105). The estimated 3-year EFS rates were 96.0% (95% CI, 88.1-98.7) versus 90.7% (95% CI, 81.5-95.6). Achieving pCR was significantly associated with improved EFS (HR = 0.15; 95% CI, 0.03-0.71; P = 0.006). Cardiac safety was comparable, with no symptomatic cardiac dysfunction and only one grade ≥3 cardiotoxicity in the EC-based sequential group. These findings support PLD-based concurrent therapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab as an effective and safe neoadjuvant option for high-risk HER2-positive breast cancer, warranting further evaluation in phase III trials.

articles.title: Hypofractionated 44 Gy in 20 fractions versus conventional chemoradiation in cervical cancer: 2-year results of the randomized HYPOCx-iRex trial with an exploratory pooled analysis of a single-institute EMBRACE-II cohort.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate 2-year late gastrointestinal (GI) toxicity, oncologic outcomes, and cost-effectiveness of hypofractionated concurrent chemoradiation with 44 Gy in 20 fractions (44 Gy/20F; HYPO) versus conventional fractionation (45 Gy/25F; CVRT + EMB) for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). METHODS: The primary analysis was the randomized HYPOCx-iRex comparison (HYPO n = 21 vs. CVRT n = 19). A pre-planned pooled analysis additionally incorporated a concurrent, nonrandomized single-institute EMBRACE-II cohort (EMB n = 28; total n = 68). Late GI toxicity was graded by CTCAEv5.0. Dose-toxicity analysis used Cox and Probit regression to identify the effective dose associated with 10% toxicity probability (ED10). The indirect ratio of excess dose volume at 60 Gy EQD2 (iRex60) was evaluated as a brachytherapy (BT) conformity index. Locoregional control (LRC) and overall survival (OS) were estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were calculated from provider and societal perspectives. RESULTS: Median overall treatment time was 39 versus 46 days in HYPO versus CVRT+EMB (p < 0.001). Late GI toxicity was numerically higher in HYPO (2-year Gr ≥2: 23.8% vs. 10.8%, pLR = 0.168; Gr ≥3: 19.1% vs. 5.3%, pLR = 0.066); iRex60 was identified as an independent predictor in multivariable regression (ED10 = 1.6 and 1.85 for Gr ≥2/Gr ≥3; proposed cut-off iRex60 <1.7). Favorable but nonsignificant trends in LRC (95.2% vs. 77.5%; HR = 0.43, pLR = 0.260) and OS (100% vs. 76.8%; HR = 0.22, pLR = 0.107) were observed. The 44Gy/20F regimen demonstrated dominant cost-effectiveness. CONCLUSION: Hypofractionated chemoradiation achieved LRC and OS comparable to conventional fractionation with shorter treatment time and lower cost. The higher late GI toxicity observed with hypofractionation is clinically meaningful without statistical significance. Further optimization of brachytherapy conformity and low-to-intermediate dose constraints is proposed before clinical adoption. The iRex60 threshold and the cost-effectiveness findings are hypothesis-generating and need further validation.

articles.title: Comparison of Postoperative Pain Following Modified Radical Mastectomy under Thoracic Epidural Anesthesia versus General Anesthesia: A Randomized Control Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast surgeries are commonly performed under general anesthesia. The aim of the study was to compare postoperative pain following modified radical mastectomy under thoracic epidural anesthesia versus general anesthesia with the use of laryngeal mask airway. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This randomized controlled study was performed on hundred patients undergoing unilateral modified radical mastectomy. The patients were assigned into two equal groups, E and G. Group E patients received thoracic epidural anaesthesia, and group G received general anesthesia. The primary objective was to compare postoperative pain scores between the two groups. Secondary objectives included incidence of postoperative sore throat, hoarseness of voice, cough, nausea and vomiting, perioperative analgesic requirement, patient and surgeon satisfaction, duration of hospital and intensive care unit (ICU) stay, and any associated anesthesia complications. RESULTS: Both groups were similar with respect to demographics. Postoperative pain score was significantly lower in Group E at all time points. The perioperative analgesic requirement was significantly higher in Group G than in Group E, and this was statistically significant with P < 0.001. Duration of hospital stay and intraoperative hemodynamics were comparable between the two groups. Patient satisfaction was significantly higher in Group G; however, surgeons were satisfied with both methods. Sore throat, cough, hoarseness of voice, nausea and vomiting, and duration of ICU stay were significantly higher in group G. Infiltration of local anesthetic in the axilla was required in 10% of the patients in the epidural group. CONCLUSIONS: Although patients found general anesthesia more satisfying, thoracic epidural anesthesia provided significantly better postoperative analgesia compared with general anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway inpatients undergoing modified radical mastectomy and was associated with significantly lower ICU stay, comparable surgeon satisfaction with lower incidence of postoperative sore throat, nausea and vomiting, hoarseness of voice, and cough. CONTEXTE:: Les chirurgies du sein sont couramment réalisées sous anesthésie générale. Le but de cette étude était de comparer la douleur postopératoire après une mastectomie radicale modifiée sous anesthésie péridurale thoracique par rapport à l’anesthésie générale avec utilisation d’un masque laryngé. MATÉRIEL ET MÉTHODES:: Cette étude randomisée et contrôlée a été réalisée sur cent patientes subissant une mastectomie radicale modifiée unilatérale. Les patientes ont été réparties en deux groupes égaux, E et G. Les patientes du groupe E ont reçu une anesthésie péridurale thoracique, et celles du groupe G une anesthésie générale. L’objectif principal était de comparer les scores de douleur postopératoire entre les deux groupes. Les objectifs secondaires comprenaient l’incidence des maux de gorge postopératoires, de l’enrouement de la voix, de la toux, des nausées et vomissements, des besoins en analgésiques peropératoires, de la satisfaction de la patiente et du chirurgien, de la durée du séjour à l’hôpital et en unité de soins intensifs (USI), ainsi que de toute complication anesthésique associée. RÉSULTATS:: Les deux groupes étaient similaires en ce qui concerne les données démographiques.1 Le score de douleur postopératoire était significativement plus faible dans le Groupe E à tous les moments. Le besoin en analgésiques peropératoires était significativement plus élevé dans le Groupe G que dans le Groupe E, et cela était statistiquement significatif avec $ CONCLUSIONS:: Bien que les patientes aient trouvé l’anesthésie générale plus satisfaisante, l’anesthésie péridurale thoracique a procuré une analgésie postopératoire significativement meilleure par rapport à l’anesthésie générale avec masque laryngé chez les patientes subissant une mastectomie radicale modifiée, et était associée à une durée de séjour en USI significativement plus courte, à une satisfaction du chirurgien comparable avec une incidence plus faible des maux de gorge postopératoires, des nausées et vomissements, de l’enrouement de la voix et de la toux.

articles.title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of the PD-1 Inhibitor Cetrelimab in Chronic Hepatitis B.
articles.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV)-induced T-cell exhaustion may be reversed using a programmed death receptor 1 (PD-1) inhibitor such as cetrelimab, an investigational fully human monoclonal antibody targeting PD-1. To evaluate the safety, activity and pharmacokinetics of low-dose (i.e., a dose lower than that used in oncology) cetrelimab in participants with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) virologically suppressed (VS) on a stable nucleos(t)ide analog (NA). Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-cohort, single-dose escalation study of cetrelimab administered subcutaneously or intravenously. Due to a strategic decision, and not to any safety concern, only one cohort (45 mg subcutaneous) was executed. Participants maintained their NA treatment to avoid HBV reactivation. Serum cetrelimab concentrations, HBV biomarkers, PD-1 receptor occupancy (RO) and safety were collected over 24 weeks. Eleven participants were enrolled and randomized, eight to cetrelimab and three to placebo and all 11 completed the study. Mean cetrelimab half-life was 16.3 days with median time to maximum cetrelimab concentration 10.4 days post-dose. Near-maximal RO was achieved 6 h post-dose which waned over time. There were no clinically relevant changes in HBV biomarkers or laboratory values including liver function tests and thyroid-stimulating hormone. No clinically relevant adverse events were reported. A single 45 mg dose of cetrelimab administered subcutaneously in VS participants with CHB was safe and well tolerated. There was no change in HBV biomarkers and further development of cetrelimab for HBV was abandoned. Clinical Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05242445; EudraCT Number: 2021-004857-21.

articles.title: Ex Vivo Thrombin Generation Assessment of Four Anticoagulants in Children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolic events (VTE) are a serious complication in children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Currently, there is no consensus regarding anticoagulant treatment or prevention in this setting, and the role of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) has not been extensively studied. The recent approval of DOACs for the treatment of VTE in children supports their further evaluation in pediatric patients with ALL. We prospectively evaluated the effects of four anticoagulant agents in 67 pediatric patients with ALL, compared with healthy controls, using the global coagulation assay thrombin generation (TG). The first 21 patients formed the calibration cohort, and we performed the primary TG analysis in the subsequent 46 patients. articles.title: Decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide versus busulfan-cyclophosphamide myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for reducing risk of relapse in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia in China: an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: An unmet need persists for optimal myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia. We investigated whether decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide (DAC-BuCy) conditioning reduced the risk of relapse compared with busulfan-cyclophosphamide (BuCy) conditioning. METHODS: In this open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial at eight transplantation centres in China, eligible patients were aged 14-65 years, had morphologically confirmed KMT2A-rearranged leukaemia, and had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-2. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) before HSCT to DAC-BuCy (intravenous decitabine 20 mg/m FINDINGS: Between May 1, 2019, and Jan 31, 2023, 130 patients were randomised to receive a DAC-BuCy (n=65; 34 [52%] female and 31 [48%] male) or BuCy (n=65; 29 [45%] female and 36 [55%] male) regimen. Median follow-up was 34·7 months (IQR 30·2-52·5). 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 12% (95% CI 6-22) in the DAC-BuCy group and 29% (19-41) in the BuCy group (hazard ratio 0·41 [0·20-0·87]; p=0·017). The most common grade 3-5 adverse events were infections or infestations (DAC-BuCy group 27 [42%] and BuCy group 25 [38%]), acute graft-versus-host disease (DAC-BuCy group 23 [35%] and BuCy group 22 [34%]), and gastrointestinal disorders (DAC-BuCy group 14 [22%] and BuCy group 15 [23%]). Four (6%) patients in the DAC-BuCy group and five (8%) patients in the BuCy group died from adverse events, of which two were due to regimen-related toxicities: one nervous system disorder in the DAC-BuCy group and one cardiac disorder in the BuCy group. INTERPRETATION: The addition of decitabine to BuCy conditioning reduced the risk of relapse with an acceptable safety profile in adult patients with KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia and could be a suitable therapeutic option for this population. FUNDING: The National Natural Science Foundation of China, the National Key Research and Development Program of China, the Science and Technology Program of Guangdong Province, the Non-communicable Chronic Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project, the Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province, the Science and Technology Planning Project of Guangzhou, and the Outstanding Youth Cultivation Program of Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University. TRANSLATION: For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

articles.title: Breast cancer screening based on clinical breast examination performed by community health workers: study protocol for a randomized clinical trial - ITABERAÍ Project.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The ITABERAÍ project evaluates whether breast cancer screening based on clinical breast examination (CBE) performed by community health workers (CHWs) can reduce advanced breast cancer and mortality. METHODS: This prospective, phase III, cluster-randomized controlled trial includes women aged ≥40 years using Brazil's public health system. Primary healthcare units and their Family Health Teams were randomized to a control group (CG) or intervention grop (IG). CHWs in the CG received standard breast cancer screening training. Female CHWs in the IG received standard training plus additional theoretical and practical training in CBE. Data collection includes sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, medical history, and CBE findings. The sample size was calculated to detect a 10% reduction in advanced cases and a 20% reduction in mortality, with 2104 per group. A pilot test from August to December 2022 validated CRFs, workflows, and the integrated data-collection system. Ethics approval was obtained (CAAE 56916522.8.0000.5078). TRIAL STATUS: The trial was initiated in January 2023. By March 2026, 4036 women had been randomized, 2056 (98%) to the control group and 1980 (94%) to the intervention group. The study runs for 16 years. Recruitment is intended to be completed in December 2026. TRIAL REGISTRATION: RBR-39vm2nd. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry (ReBEC) RBR-39vm2nd; registered on 12 March 2023. https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-39vm2nd.

articles.title: Matching-adjusted indirect comparison of zanubrutinib and real-world chemotherapy, rituximab and chemoimmunotherapy in relapsed or refractory marginal zone lymphoma.
articles.abstract: What is this article about? Marginal zone lymphoma is a type of blood cancer. Some patients experience relapsed or refractory disease, meaning the cancer returns or does not respond to treatment. Common treatments include chemotherapy, rituximab or chemoimmunotherapy (CIT). Zanubrutinib is a targeted therapy that has shown promising results in clinical trials, but it has not been directly compared with these traditional treatments in a randomized study. What were the results? Researchers compared data from clinical trials of zanubrutinib with real-world data from patients with marginal zone lymphoma who received chemotherapy, rituximab or CIT. Statistical methods were used to balance baseline patient differences between treatment groups. After matching, patients treated with zanubrutinib had longer survival than patients treated with traditional therapies. Results remained consistent in additional analyses comparing to rituximab or CIT alone. What do the results mean? These findings suggest that zanubrutinib may provide better outcomes than traditional treatment approaches for patients with relapsed or refractory marginal zone lymphoma. This study also shows how clinical trial and real-world data can be combined to help compare treatments when head-to-head studies are not available.

articles.title: Daratumumab, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma: MAIA final survival analysis.
articles.abstract: In previous analyses of MAIA, daratumumab plus lenalidomide/dexamethasone (D-Rd) significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival (OS) versus lenalidomide/dexamethasone (Rd) in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM). We report results on long-term OS and subsequent antimyeloma therapies from the MAIA final analysis. A protocol amendment (July 20, 2021) led to a long-term extension of MAIA, during which patients were followed for OS. A total of 737 patients were randomized to D-Rd (n = 368) or Rd (n = 369). At a median follow-up of 89.3 months (range, 0.0-102.2; interquartile range, 85.3-93.0), median OS was 90.3 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 80.8-not estimable [NE]) with D-Rd versus 64.1 months (56.0-70.8) with Rd (hazard ratio [HR], 0.67; 95% CI, 0.55-0.82); estimated 7-year OS rates were 53.1% (95% CI, 47.8-58.2) and 39.3% (34.1-44.5), respectively. Median time to subsequent antimyeloma treatment was not reached (95% CI, 84.1-NE) for D-Rd versus 42.4 months (33.5-50.6) for Rd (HR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.41-0.63; P < 0.0001). Death due to adverse events occurred in 84 patients (D-Rd, n = 44/364 [12%]; Rd, n = 40/365 [11%]). With >7 years of follow-up, D-Rd demonstrated a new benchmark for median OS (7.5 years) in transplant-ineligible NDMM, further supporting frontline D-Rd use to maximize survival.

articles.title: A Trial-Level Benefit-Toxicity Mapping Framework for Adjuvant Therapy in Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Focused Review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adjuvant systemic therapy for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) has evolved from vascular endothelial growth factor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (VEGF-TKIs) to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and emerging combination strategies. However, the interpretation of adjuvant trial results requires consideration not only of disease-free survival (DFS) benefit but also of severe toxicity, treatment discontinuation, comparator structure, and trial risk composition. METHODS: We conducted a focused review of randomized Phase III adjuvant RCC trials identified through PubMed and prespecified publicly available trial reports. Peer-reviewed trials were included in the primary evidence set, and contemporary conference reports were incorporated as an exploratory update. Trial-level data were extracted for efficacy, grade ≥ 3 adverse events (AEs), AE-driven and patient-initiated treatment discontinuation, and protocol-defined risk composition. A descriptive benefit-toxicity mapping framework was used to visualize DFS benefit, treatment-limiting toxicity, severe AE burden, and high-risk patient proportion without implying indirect treatment ranking. RESULTS: Nine peer-reviewed trial programs and one conference-only report were included. TKI-based trials showed limited and inconsistent DFS benefit, with only S-TRAC meeting its primary endpoint, while grade ≥ 3 AE burden was consistently high (60%-72%) and patient-initiated discontinuation was frequent. Among ICI-based trials, KEYNOTE-564 showed DFS benefit, whereas IMmotion010 and CheckMate 914 Part A were negative. RAMPART (conference report) and LITESPARK-022 showed additional DFS signals with ICI-based combinations, accompanied by AE-driven discontinuation in approximately one-third of patients, with important differences in risk composition and comparator design. CONCLUSIONS: Trial-level benefit-toxicity mapping contextualizes adjuvant RCC trials by integrating DFS benefit, toxicity burden, treatment-limiting events, and risk composition, without implying direct cross-trial ranking.

articles.title: An evaluation of retifanlimab-dlwr with carboplatin and paclitaxel and as a single agent for squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Anal squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is a rare cancer. Metastatic anal SCC is still a significant clinical challenge due to limited treatment options and poor outcomes. AREAS COVERED: This review paper will focus on retifanlimab, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting the programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) pathway, and its role in the treatment of metastatic anal SCC, both as monotherapy or in combination with chemotherapy. This review will evaluate its efficacy, safety, and place within the current therapeutic landscape. EXPERT OPINION: The POD1UM-303 trial is the first randomized phase III study for patients with metastatic and locally, advanced unresectable anal SCC. The results from POD1UM-303 are practice-changing, establishing retifanlimab in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel as a new standard of care for first-line treatment in this setting. Current research includes investigating earlier integration of PD-(L)1 inhibitors with definitive chemoradiotherapy in the locally advanced setting. Further biomarker-driven studies are essential to guide treatment and improve patient selection.

articles.title: Phase III Study of Niraparib Plus Pembrolizumab as Maintenance Therapy for Advanced or Metastatic NSCLC (ZEAL-1L).
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This randomized, double-blind, phase 3 study evaluated niraparib plus pembrolizumab as maintenance therapy for patients with advanced or metastatic NSCLC (NSCLC; ZEAL-1L, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04475939). METHODS: Adults with advanced or metastatic squamous or nonsquamous NSCLC without a known targetable driver alteration were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive niraparib plus pembrolizumab or placebo plus pembrolizumab as maintenance therapy. Niraparib was given as a daily oral dose of 300 or 200 mg, and intravenous pembrolizumab was administered at 200 mg every 3 weeks. The primary end point was progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review in patients with a complete or partial response (CR/PR) to front-line chemotherapy combined with pembrolizumab. Hierarchical testing was performed on the primary and key secondary end points in a prespecified sequential order; formal testing was stopped if any end point failed to reach statistical significance. RESULTS: Patients comprising the intent-to-treat (ITT) population (n = 666) were randomly assigned to niraparib plus pembrolizumab (n = 331) or placebo-plus-pembrolizumab (n = 335) therapy. The median PFS for the CR/PR population (n = 200 receiving niraparib plus pembrolizumab; n = 201 receiving placebo-plus-pembrolizumab) was 5.55 months in both treatment arms (hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% confidence interval: 0.79-1.27; 1-sided p = 0.502). Key secondary end points of PFS by blinded independent central review in the ITT population, overall survival in the CR/PR and ITT populations, and time to progression in the central nervous system were not formally tested. The most common grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events in the niraparib plus pembrolizumab arm were hematologic (anemia, thrombocytopenia, and neutropenia). CONCLUSION: The addition of niraparib to pembrolizumab for maintenance therapy in patients with advanced or metastatic NSCLC did not result in improved efficacy; no new safety signals were detected. CLINICAL TRIAL INFORMATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04475939.

articles.title: Disease-free survival and overall survival after neoadjuvant immunotherapy in mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer in the Netherlands: results of the single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade induces high pathological response rates in patients with locally advanced mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) colon cancer, yet long-term survival outcomes have not been established. Previously, we reported safety (a primary endpoint) and pathological response (a secondary endpoint) data from the NICHE-2 trial. Here, we report the primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival and the exploratory endpoint of 5-year overall survival. METHODS: In this single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial, patients with previously untreated, clinical stage 2 or 3, resectable dMMR colon cancer received a single dose of intravenous ipilimumab (1 mg per kg) on day 1, and two doses of intravenous nivolumab (3 mg per kg) on days 1 and 15, followed by surgery in one of the six participating hospitals in the Netherlands. Here, we report the independent primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival (time from surgery until disease recurrence or death from any cause) and the secondary endpoint of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) analysis. Overall survival (time from study enrolment until death from any cause) is reported as an exploratory post-hoc analysis. All endpoints were assessed in the per-protocol population (patients who met the eligibility criteria and received at least one cycle of therapy). The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03026140, and has completed accrual. FINDINGS: From July 4, 2017, to July 18, 2022, 123 patients were screened, of whom 115 were treated and 111 were included in the per-protocol population. At the data cutoff (June 19, 2026), the postoperative median follow-up was 58·7 months (IQR 49·0-72·9). The 3-year disease-free survival was 100% (97·5% CI 100-100). After a median follow-up of 60·4 months (IQR 50·6-74·1), calculated from time of study enrolment, the 5-year overall survival was 100% (95% CI 100-100). In patients with available plasma samples, ctDNA was detected in 99 (92%) of 108 patients at baseline, and ctDNA clearance was observed in 44 (45%) of 98 patients after the first cycle in week 2 and in 80 (82%) of 97 patients after the second cycle before surgery. In patients with a pathological near-complete response and complete response, presurgery ctDNA clearance was observed in 19 (70%) of 27 patients and 60 (92%) of 65 patients, respectively. Assessment for minimal residual disease after surgery revealed that all patients were ctDNA negative. INTERPRETATION: In patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer, treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery resulted in a 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival of 100%. These findings support neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a potential standard of care for patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer. FUNDING: Bristol Myers Squibb.

articles.title: Resistance training and protein supplementation in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer: a randomized feasibility trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Cancer cachexia is associated with reduced physical performance, quality of life, and survival in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer. Resistance training and protein supplementation have the potential to improve these outcomes. Whether an intervention comprising resistance training and protein supplementation is feasible during treatment for incurable gastroesophageal cancer is not known. METHODS: This was an open-label, parallel-group, two-arm, randomized controlled feasibility trial. Patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer scheduled to undergo first-line chemotherapy were randomized 2:1 to resistance training three times per week and daily protein supplementation or to control. The primary outcome, feasibility, was assessed by recruitment, retention, adherence, and harms. Secondary outcomes included body composition, physical performance, quality of life, and treatment tolerability. RESULTS: Out of 106 potentially eligible patients, 20 participants (5 female and 15 male, mean age 65) were randomized yielding a recruitment rate of 19%. 18 participants completed the trial with a retention rate of 90%. Median (25th; 75th percentile) adherence to the resistance training sessions and to the protein supplements was 63% (43; 77) and 39% (17; 76), respectively. Five participants (38%) met the minimum feasibility criteria of both interventions. No serious adverse events related to the intervention occurred. We found no between-group differences in body composition, physical performance, quality of life, or treatment tolerability. CONCLUSION: Resistance training combined with protein supplementation was not feasible during first-line chemotherapy in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer due to low accrual and low adherence to protein supplementation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05650827. Study registration date 2022-12-12.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

articles.title: Effect of Duloxetine on the Perioperative Anxiety Status and Stress Response Following Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The impact of psychological factors on surgical stress response has garnered extensive attention. However, perioperative intervention strategies are still lacking for the total hip arthroplasty (THA) population without psychiatric comorbidities. This study aimed to assess the efficacy of duloxetine in perioperative anxiety status and stress response in these patients. METHODS: This was a double-blind randomized controlled trial conducted between September 2021 and August 2024. Eligible patients aged over 18 years scheduled for unilateral primary total hip arthroplasty were recruited, with exclusion of patients with diagnosed mental diseases, endocrine disorders, previous psychiatric medication use, or severe hepatorenal dysfunction. A computer-generated random sequence was used to assign 100 patients to either the duloxetine group or the placebo group. The patients received 60 mg of duloxetine or the placebo daily starting 2 days before the surgery to postoperative day two. The primary outcome was the anxiety status assessed using the Hamilton anxiety scale (HAMA). The self-rating anxiety scale (SAS), stress response-related inflammatory levels and neuroendocrine levels, visual analog scale (VAS), patient satisfaction, quality of recovery-15 (QoR-15) score, Harris hip score (HHS), University of California Los Angeles (UCLA) activity score, and adverse effects were also compared. Continuous outcomes with multiple time points were analyzed using linear mixed models, while single time point outcomes used t-test or Mann-Whitney U test. Preoperative to POD1 differences were assessed with paired t-test or Wilcoxon test. Categorical variables and response rate were analyzed using chi-square or Fisher's exact test. Correlation analysis examined anxiety and stress biomarker relationships. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: The duloxetine group had significantly lower HAMA and SAS scores than the placebo group on POD2 (both p < 0.05). The VAS score during walking was significantly lower in the duloxetine group (p < 0.05). Patients in the duloxetine group exhibited higher QoR-15, HHS, and UCLA scores and better satisfaction (all p < 0.05). The erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio (NLR), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α), adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), plasma cortisol (PTC), and blood glucose (BG) were significantly lower in the duloxetine group (all p < 0.05). The ESR and HAMA, ACTH and SAS, and PTC and SAS were respectively correlated (all p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: The perioperative administration of duloxetine alleviated anxiety, reduced postoperative walking pain, improved the quality of functional recovery and satisfaction, and may reduce the stress response in patients undergoing THA. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trial Register: ChiCTR2100051099.

articles.title: Prognostic impact of diabetes or hypertension in smokers with CRPC receiving enzalutamide or abiraterone.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Smoking and lifestyle‑related diseases increase the risk of cancer incidence and progression, but their impact on castration‑resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) remains unclear. This study examined whether diabetes mellitus (DM), hypertension (HT), and smoking habit (SH) affect the prognosis of CRPC patients treated with enzalutamide (ENZ) or abiraterone plus prednisolone (ABI). METHODS: Using data from the ENABLE study for PCa, an investigator‑initiated, multicenter, randomized controlled trial, patients were retrospectively categorized into two groups based on SH. Subsequently, the impact of the absence or presence of either DM or HT and treatment arm (ENZ or ABI) on survival endpoints was investigated. RESULTS: A total of 178 patients were randomized and treated, of whom 161 had available SH information and were included in the analysis (84 SH- and 77 SH+). No significant differences in survival endpoints were observed between the SH- and SH+ groups. In the SH+ group, prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS) was significantly worse in the with‑DM/HT group than in the no‑DM/HT group (p = 0.0215). Multivariate Cox analysis confirmed that the presence of DM or HT was an independent predictor of poor PCSS. Furthermore, a significant difference in PCSS between the no‑DM/HT and with‑DM/HT groups was observed in the ENZ arm (p = 0.0201), but not in the ABI arm. CONCLUSIONS: SH does not appear to influence the efficacy of ENZ or ABI therapy for CRPC; however, among SH+ patients, the presence of DM or HT was associated with poorer survival outcomes, particularly in those treated with ENZ.

articles.title: Long-term local recurrence and survival after colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection: a prospective multicenter real-world cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Information on long-term outcomes of colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) in real-world clinical practice remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate long-term local recurrence and its predictors after colorectal ESD. METHODS: This prospective, multicenter study was conducted at 11 institutions in Hiroshima, Japan, and included all consecutive colorectal ESD cases (1838 lesions from 1732 patients) between 2014 and 2018. The primary outcome was the cumulative local recurrence rate. The secondary outcomes included factors associated with local recurrence, overall survival, and cancer-specific survival. Factors associated with local recurrence were evaluated using cause-specific Cox proportional hazards models using Firth's penalized partial likelihood. RESULTS: The cumulative local recurrence rates at 1, 3, and 5 years were 0.06%, 0.64%, and 0.75%, respectively. The longest interval to recurrence was 52 months. No local recurrence was observed in patients who achieved curative resection. Rectal lesions (hazard ratio [HR] 3.93; P = 0.04), high-risk pathologic features (HR 14.3; P < 0.001), R1 resection (HR 7.59; P = 0.003), and delayed bleeding (HR 7.72; P = 0.009) were associated with local recurrence. The 5-year overall survival and cancer-specific survival rates were 95.3% and 100%, respectively; however, 1/10 patients with local recurrence developed liver and lung metastases and subsequently died 64 months after ESD. CONCLUSIONS: Colorectal ESD had a very low long-term local recurrence rate in real-world clinical settings. No recurrence was observed in patients who underwent curative resection. Long-term surveillance is warranted after noncurative resection.

articles.title: Effect of Personalized Risk Messages on Patient Intent and Decision Making in Colorectal Cancer Screening: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: PurposeTo measure the impact of a personalized message about current risk of having advanced colorectal neoplasia (ACN; colorectal cancer [CRC] or advanced precancerous polyp) on informed concordance and CRC screening decision-making outcomes.MethodsA total of 1,084 patients, aged 50 to 75 y, with an upcoming clinic appointment, due for CRC screening, and at average risk for CRC were randomized to view a decision aid (DA) about CRC screening with or without personalized ACN risk information. Providers were randomized to receive CRC screening notifications with or without each patient's personalized ACN risk. Patients completed surveys before (T0), immediately after viewing the DA (T1), and after their clinic visit (T2) to assess informed concordance (primary outcome), screening intent, decisional conflict, knowledge, perceived personal risk, and perceived shared decision making. Analysis of covariance and logistic regression models compared intended screening behavior and decision-making outcomes by intervention groups.ResultsAt T1, participants (mean age 56.5 y, 59.7% female) sent the personalized rather than the generic DA had higher odds of intending to be screened with any test (odds ratio [OR] = 1.55, confidence interval [CI] = 1.03, 2.33) and to have a stool test (OR = 2.17, CI = 1.62, 2.91) and lower odds of intending to undergo colonoscopy (OR = 0.58, CI = 0.43, 0.79). There were no statistically significant effects of either intervention on informed concordance. Moderation analysis, however, showed that for one health system, participants whose provider was sent the personalized notification had higher odds of informed concordance.LimitationsSingle Midwestern city, English-speaking patients only, low enrollment of patients at high-average risk for ACN.ConclusionProviding patients with a personalized message about their ACN risk increased the intent to be screened and to do a stool test and decreased the intent to undergo colonoscopy. For one health system, sending providers the ACN risk message increased the odds of informed concordance.ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04683731HighlightsA personalized message about patients' advanced colorectal neoplasia (ACN) risk, provided as part of a decision aid, increased patients' intent to be screened with any test and to have a stool test and decreased their intent to be screened with colonoscopy.A personalized message about patients' ACN risk, included in a decision aid sent to patients or in a screening notification sent to their providers, had no significant effect on informed concordance.At one health system, a personalized message sent to providers about their patients' ACN risk increased the odds of informed concordance between the patients' intended screening test and the test received.
articles.journal: Medical decision making : an international journal of the Society for Medical Decision Making

articles.title: Can Esophagectomy be Safely Avoided After Clinical Complete Response in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma? Response Assessment, Active Surveillance, and Salvage in the Immunotherapy Era.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Clinical complete response (cCR) after chemoradiotherapy or immunotherapy-containing neoadjuvant treatment is increasingly encountered in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). We examine whether esophagectomy can be safely deferred or avoided in selected complete responders, distinguishing prediction of pathologic complete response (pCR) from the higher confidence required to omit surgery. RECENT FINDINGS: The phase III SANO trial showed non-inferior 2-year overall survival with active surveillance versus standard surgery after cCR following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, with early quality-of-life benefits; however, approximately three quarters of participants had adenocarcinoma. The ESCC-specific preSINO study showed that bite-on-bite biopsies, endoscopic ultrasonography with fine-needle aspiration, and PET/CT reduce but do not eliminate missed residual disease. In a biomarker analysis nested within preSINO, adding tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) to conventional evaluation increased sensitivity for non-pCR to approximately 92-93%; this is not independent validation. Neoadjuvant immunotherapy, including ESCORT-NEO and PALACE regimens, has increased pCR rates, but response-assessment accuracy has not been validated in these treatment contexts. Earlier ESCC trials of definitive chemoradiotherapy with selective salvage established organ preservation conceptually; the modern question is whether surveillance can be individualized after rigorously defined cCR. Active surveillance after cCR is now a credible option within structured programs, but routine omission of esophagectomy in ESCC is not yet standard care. Organ preservation should be viewed as a longitudinal residual-disease exclusion program with predefined rescue triggers rather than a one-time declaration of cCR. ESCC-specific, treatment-context-specific trials integrating standardized endoscopic and nodal assessment, PET/CT, serial ctDNA, and salvage outcomes are needed before immunotherapy-associated cCR can routinely justify nonoperative management.

articles.title: Longitudinal remodeling of the tumor-immune microenvironment during regorafenib, nivolumab, and chemotherapy in advanced gastric cancer.
articles.abstract: Previous studies combining the multikinase inhibitor regorafenib with a PD-1 inhibitor showed promising activity in gastric cancer. We conducted a phase 1b/2 trial (NCT05394740) of first-line regorafenib, nivolumab, and chemotherapy in 30 patients with mismatch repair-proficient gastric cancer and investigated its impact on the tumor microenvironment. The primary end point was met; 22 of 30 patients showed objective tumor response (73%; 80% confidence interval, 60.3 to 83.8). Single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing were performed on biopsy samples at baseline, during treatment, and at disease progression. The combination treatment increased tumor antigen-reactive CD8

articles.title: CEA-targeted fluorescence endoscopy for the detection of high-grade dysplasia and early invasive rectal cancer: A proof-of-concept trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Accurate recognition of high-grade dysplasia (HGD) and early invasive carcinoma (IC) within colorectal polyps is essential for selecting the preferred local resection technique. However, optical endoscopic diagnosis can be challenging, particularly in large and advanced polyps. This study investigates whether carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA)-targeted near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) imaging can distinguish polyps containing HGD/IC from polyps solely containing low-grade dysplasia (LGD), given prior evidence of CEA overexpression in HGD/IC relative to LGD. METHODS: Patients scheduled for local en-bloc endoscopic resection of advanced rectal polyps were included in the study and received 5 mg or 10 mg intravenous SGM-101, a CEA-targeted fluorescent agent. In vivo imaging was performed using a rigid Quest-Olympus NIRF-endoscope, followed by ex vivo whole-specimen and bread-loaf imaging using the PEARL imaging system.
